title: Great Britain Smashes Ecuador to Reach Davis Cup Finals!
summary: How do you win a tennis match when your best players are injured? You call up your backups — and they deliver! Great Britain beat Ecuador 4-0 to reach the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023. The winning moment came when Henry Patten and Neal Skupski won their doubles match 6-3, 6-4 at London's Copper Box Arena. That gave Britain a 3-0 lead, and Harry Wendelken finished the job with a 6-2, 6-3 win in his first-ever Davis Cup match. He was a late replacement for Cameron Norrie, who hurt his arm in practice. Britain's team was missing several top players. Jack Draper ended his season early, and two others were injured. But Toby Samuel, 24, fought back from a set down to win his debut match. Arthur Fery also won easily. The doubles team didn't even face a single break point. 'To do it in three straight rubbers is really good,' said captain Leon Smith. Now Britain heads to Bologna, Italy, for the Final 8 in November. They'll face tough teams, but Smith says they have a chance. 'You try and steal one of the singles, and it goes to the doubles and you've got a good doubles team,' he said. Sounds like a plan!
why_it_matters: It shows that a team can still win when its biggest stars are missing, because the players who normally wait on the bench are ready to step up.

background_read: The Davis Cup is an international men's tennis competition where countries play against each other, and it has been running since 1900.
In the Davis Cup, teams play 'ties' over a few days: each tie is made of singles and doubles matches, and each individual match is called a 'rubber'.
Great Britain has one of the oldest tennis traditions in the world and has won the Davis Cup many times, most recently in 2015.
Article_Structure: WHO: Great Britain's Davis Cup team, led by captain Leon Smith, including Henry Patten, Neal Skupski and first-time players Harry Wendelken, Toby Samuel and Arthur Fery.
WHAT: Britain beat Ecuador 4-0 to reach the Davis Cup Finals for the first time since 2023.
WHERE: At London's Copper Box Arena, with the Final 8 coming up in Bologna, Italy in November.
WHY: Several top players were injured or absent, so the backups had to step in — and they won every match.

perspectives.description: They are thrilled that the team reached the Finals even without its biggest stars, and proud of the new players who won on their first try.
They are disappointed with the loss, but they were facing a very deep British squad that was also playing at home in London.
They point out that strong teams often win because of their backups, not just their stars — team depth is what carries a country through a long competition.
